notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Cass County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($200,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to North Dakota local candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-12. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for North Dakota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The West Fargo Police Department has 47 Flock Safety automated license plate readers.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS007012, citing KFGO

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.vendor: North Dakota Bureau of Criminal Investigation
redFlags.detail: The West Fargo Police Department can run face recognition requests through the North Dakota Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system. The agency submitted three requests through the Bureau of Criminal Investigation's face recognition system between March 2023 to October 2024.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012178, citing Bureau Of Criminal Investigation Division of North Dakota

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.detail: The West Fargo Police Department paid $1,000 to Clearview AI for face recognition services in 2020.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS011508, citing City of West Fargo

redFlags.label: Private camera registry
redFlags.detail: The West Fargo Police Department started a camera registry in 2015 called the "Citizens Electronic Eye" program.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS002926, citing Inforum

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Red River Valley UAS Unit operates eight DJI drones as of 2019, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College. The unit is comprised of staff from the Fargo Fire Department, Fargo Police Department, West Fargo Fire Department, West Fargo Police Department, and the Cass County Sheriff's Office
